reviewer_notes: Agreed after discussion. Position and time consequences are reviewed in separate mirrored harm records; the adjudication coding remains unchanged.
Approved as the mirrored official decision for the shared incident; retain the shared incident ID for clustered and deduplicated sensitivity analyses.
Adjudication approved as coded. Damage to both cars is a separate harm question; Gasly's earlier contact with Car 11 confounds attribution of his later pace loss.
Adjudication approved as coded. Create and independently review a separate Norris harm assessment before making claims about the contact's realized time or position cost.

Adjudication approved as coded against the corrected official 2025 F1 guideline source. Create and independently review a separate Colapinto harm assessment; current evidence supports time lost but not a quantified position loss, repair stop, or collision-attributable damage.

Adjudication approved as coded. Add a separately reviewed low or transient harm observation for Bearman to retain non-severe outcomes in the denominator; he passed Colapinto on the following lap and no contact damage or forced stop was identified.

Adjudication approved as mitigated and guideline-conformant. Preserve the location as between Turns 3 and 4 rather than forcing one turn value. Add a separately reviewed Piastri harm record classified as potentially race-material but not proven outcome-changing.

Adjudication approved as coded. Add a separately reviewed race-ending Verstappen harm record and evaluate the championship-material but uncertain lost-points counterfactual. Also measure the realized effect of Antonelli's carried-over three-place grid penalty and other delayed punishments rather than treating their nominal values as their effects.

Adjudication approved as coded. Retain Stroll's observed one-position loss only as a descriptive no-fault competitive outcome and exclude it from harm-versus-sanction proportionality calculations. Treat accessible Document 46 as the single controlling decision rather than double-counting the earlier unavailable document.

Impact approved as coded. Because the five-second penalty was added to the final classification, removing it mechanically moves Perez from P4 to P2, restores six standard points, and changes the podium without requiring behavioral or strategy assumptions.

Impact approved as coded. Removing the post-race five-second addition leaves Colapinto 3.230 seconds behind Stroll, so the sanction had zero realized position and championship-point effect despite its nominal time and licence-point burden.

Impact approved as not mechanically estimable. Retain the confirmed ten-second stationary hold and observed P15-to-P16 stop sequence, but do not attribute the position change solely to the penalty because an ordinary stop likely also lost the place and the no-penalty strategy could have omitted the stop.

Impact approved as not estimable for Austrian finish or points. Implement a separately sourced cross-event sanction record for Silverstone: Antonelli qualified P7 and started P10, an exact three-place grid effect; the wet-race finish and points effect remains not estimable because of strategy, neutralizations, a separate collision, and retirement.

Harm assessment approved as coded. The P1-to-P2 change and 1.683-second relative swing are observed competitive effects of the complete battle and pass, not collision-damage estimates. No repair stop or confirmed lasting damage was identified; one clean post-incident lap is insufficient for persistent-pace inference.

Mirrored outcome assessment approved as coded. Verstappen's P2-to-P1 change and 1.683-second relative gain describe the completed battle and pass, not a causal benefit from contact. The shared incident ID preserves both driver perspectives while preventing the pair from being counted as two independent incidents.
